title: Your relationship is ending and you have to say it
lede: You have known for a while. There is a shared home, maybe children, maybe money, and a person who does not know that today is the day. Every version of the sentence sounds cruel.

blocks.text: You have known for a while. There is a shared home, maybe children, maybe money, and a person who does not know that today is the day. Every version of the sentence sounds cruel.

items: Kindness here is clarity, not softness. A vague ending leaves them negotiating with a decision that is already final, which is a much worse thing to do to someone.
You have had months of private processing that they have not had. Their reaction is to news; yours is to a conclusion. That asymmetry is the source of most of the mess.
The instinct to soften it with hope — "maybe in the future," "let us see" — is about your discomfort, not their welfare.
Logistics will dominate the following weeks. Deciding them badly in the first emotional 48 hours creates problems that last years.

items.detail: Private, at home if it is safe, not before work, not on a birthday, not in a restaurant where they cannot cry.

items.move: Say the decision in the first thirty seconds
items.detail: Do not build up through a long preamble. It is crueller because they work it out mid-sentence.

items.move: Be clear that it is a decision, not a discussion
items.detail: If it is genuinely final, say so. If it is not, do not have this conversation yet.

items.move: Give one honest reason and stop
items.detail: Not a catalogue of faults. One true reason is enough and the list becomes something they carry for a decade.

items.move: Then be quiet and let them react
items.detail: Anger, tears, bargaining, questions. Do not manage or correct it. Absorb it.

items.move: Agree only the immediate logistics tonight
items.detail: Where each of you sleeps and what you tell people. Everything else waits until both of you can think.

items.say: "I need to tell you something and I am going to say it plainly. I have decided to end our relationship."
"I have not been happy for a long time and I have stopped believing that changes. That is about me and us, and I am not going to pretend otherwise."
"I know you want me to say maybe. I am not going to, because it would not be true and it would keep you waiting."
"Let us just sort tonight. I will sleep in the spare room. We can talk about everything else at the weekend."

items: Doing it by message, or on a holiday, or before an important day of theirs.
Blaming them entirely, or blaming nobody. Both are dishonest in different directions.
Sleeping together in the days after to soften it. It resets their clock and stops nothing.
Announcing it to friends and family before they have processed it.
Doing it because of an argument, if the argument is not the reason.
Write down what needs deciding: housing, money, children, pets, dates. Deal with them as a list, not as a fight.
Get advice early if there are children or joint finances. Early advice is cheap and late advice is not.
Set a contact rule and hold it. Constant contact after a breakup causes most of the prolonged damage.
Expect to grieve too, even as the person who ended it. That surprises people and it is normal.

limit: If you are afraid of how they will react — if there has been violence, threats, or control — do not have this conversation alone or at home. The period around leaving carries the highest risk. Contact a domestic abuse service first and plan it with them.
